full_judgment:
6. Mr. Ahmed Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for accused petitioner Sayed Ahmed submits that the statutory period of limitation should be counted from 8-4-85 on which date the learned Sessions Judge received the record of the case from the Upazila Magistrate, that even if the period during which the Zonal Martial Law Administrator Zone C, Chittagong Cantonment took the present case and kept it with him from 24-11-85 to 11-12-85 and 5 days on which the Sessions Judge remained on leave and the Session Court's vacation of 30 days are excluded, even then more than 150 working days had expired before 1-3-86 and therefore the accused petitioner ought to have been released because Ordinance No. 23 of 1986 amending section 339C(2) Cr. P.C. substituting for the words none hundred twenty days' the words two hundred forty days" came into force on 27.3.86. 

 7. Mr. Q. A. Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney-General and Mr. Zahurul Huq appearing respectively for the State and the informant submit that as the accused persons did not appear on the date of the receipt of the record of the case and as the case was not ready for trial till 22.5.85 when the Government Advocate was appointed for defending the undefended accused persons, and also because the days on which the accused persons did not appear before the court due to which the trial could not be held, none of these days Can be counted as working days of the court and submits that when the  Zonal Martial Law Administrator (supra-Constitutional authority) by his order dated 24-11-85 took away the case completely out of jurisdiction of the court of Sessions as the then supreme authority the Sessions case from that date, that is, 24.11.85 ceases to be a pending Seasons case under the Cr. P.C. and cannot be treated as a case pending before the court of Sessions under the Cr. P.C. We find sub-stance in this submission. The effect of the case Supra-Constitutional authority such as Zonal Martial Law Administrator, Zone C, Chittagong Cantonment in taking away the present Sessions case from the jurisdiction of the ordinary court such as the Sessions Court is that the case ceased to be pending before the court of Sessions and when the case was sent back again by the Martial Law authority on 11-12-85 to the Sessions Judge the limitation of 150 days as provided in Section 339C(4) Cr. P.C. shall be counted afresh from that date, of course again excluding the period during which the records have been lying in this court on being called for. We, therefore, think that the accused petitioner has not acquired the right to be released under section 339C(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
